notes: The sky pairs (2026-10-23): gunships, anti-air and the eyes that fly. Authored relationships with C/B/A camp talks; tools/author_bonds_v1.py merges them into support_web.json (authored edges) and camp_talks.json / camp_talks_authored.json (generated=false). Edit here, then run the tool.

motifs: the gunship and the saint who shoots gunships

C.title: Silhouette
beats: The Archangel's barrels track the Roughneck all the way in to land. Nobody asked them to.
You can stop aiming at me. I'm parked.
Everything with rotors is a prayer I haven't answered yet.
Then keep yours low over my pad.

B.title: Learning the shape
beats: Kettle has chalked a Roughneck's outline on the Archangel's hull. Crossed through, then uncrossed.
It's the shape I don't shoot. I keep practising not shooting it.
It's harder than shooting. Fly where I can see you and it gets easier.

A.title: Under the roof
beats: After the drop, the Roughneck sat out the enemy flak inside Kettle's umbrella for a whole minute.
Their fighters peeled off when they saw who was under me.
They saw a chainsaw with wings over a gunship. Nobody argues with that.
The sky is nobody's. The little bit over you is mine.

motifs: the debt of the last sky

C.title: The bill
beats: Nox will not sit where Ceil's shadow falls.
Still paying for the last sky.
I flew that sortie. I know what it cost.
You know what it cost you. I hold the rest of the invoice.

B.title: Instalments
beats: Ceil has started landing beside the Umbrella and saying nothing, which is the most Ceil has ever said.
Forty-one names and a launch I didn't stop.
Then I'll fly cover over every launch you're near. Count it as an instalment.
Debt doesn't take instalments. It takes years.

A.title: Paid in sky
beats: The missile came in high. The Umbrella took it. The Roughneck had already cleared the bombers that would have followed.
That was the shape of the last sky. Except we won it.
It's still there. It's just not mine alone anymore.

C.title: A house with no roof
beats: Fatboy's crew watches the sky the way people watch weather.
House learned to knock. Never learned to duck.

B.title: Shingles
beats: The Archangel now parks a little behind the Fatboy, always on the bombers' side.
Your shells are loud. They bring company.
Then I'll keep answering the door upstairs.

A.title: The whole house
beats: Three bombing runs, three burning wrecks, one Fatboy still knocking.
That's the point of a roof.
House has a roof now. Feels like a home.

motifs: who owns the sky over the pad
the circle and the saint who wanders

C.title: Whose sky
beats: Warder has drawn the pad's circle in the dirt again. Kettle has driven through it again.
Owns a circle of dirt. And the air above it.
The air goes where the fight goes. So do I.
Then the pad is naked every time you wander.

B.title: Shifts
beats: They have started taking the sky in shifts, and arguing about the handover.
Your ferrets cover the pad. I cover the march.
My ferrets don't chase. They stay.
That's why I trust them with what I leave behind.

A.title: Two roofs
beats: A bomber wing came for the pad while the Archangel was out on the line. It never reached the circle.
You did. I came back because I wanted to see it hold.
Go wander. The circle will be here.

C.title: Through the flak
beats: Two of Noctua's drones came home with Archangel burns.
Dreams in flight paths. Yours went through mine.
Mine go where the enemy is. Yours were in the way.
Then teach them where the way is.

B.title: Lanes
beats: Kettle has painted the drone lanes on Noctua's bay wall: where the flak goes, and where it never goes.
Fly the cold lanes. I'll keep them cold.
They're learning. They hum when they pass you now.

A.title: Swarm hymn
beats: Twenty-four drones and an Archangel fought one sky together and did not touch once.
They fly around your fire like it's weather.
It is weather. You taught them to read it.

motifs: spot meets siege, from the sky

C.title: From up there
beats: Mira wants to know what napalm looks like from altitude.
Napalm is confetti. Tell me it's prettier from up there.
It's a map. You colour it in.

B.title: Spotting
beats: The Roughneck now flies a lazy circle over Mira's targets before the Barrage speaks.
Left of the ridge, two depots, one gun.
You're the best spotter I've ever had. You never ask me to stop.
I'm a gunship. I don't know the word.

A.title: Fireworks
beats: The barrage walked exactly where the Roughneck's tracers pointed, and then a little further for joy.
From up here it looked like a festival.
It was. You were the guest of honour.

C.title: The tally
beats: Volt and Ceil keep score on the same board. Neither agreed to it.
Sight is a wound you give them. I gave seven today.
Six of those were already burning when I flew off them.

B.title: Same burnout
beats: Both came back with redlined engines and nothing left in the tank.
You drive like me. With rotors.
One of us should learn to stop.

A.title: Shared kills
beats: The board says fourteen. It doesn't say whose.
I stopped counting which were mine.
Me too. Turns out it's faster when you don't.

C.title: Hangar kids
beats: Commando's Hercules pilot and Ceil came up in the same hangar. It shows.
You mined the hangar door once. Before the argument.

B.title: The drop
beats: The Hercules dropped Commando's crew behind a line the Roughneck had just emptied.
You were early. That's the same as being late, but louder.

A.title: Family business
beats: Mines, a drop, a gunship pass. Nobody on the other side ever saw the whole of it.
We should do this for money.
Then we should do it for fun. It's better for fun.

motifs: rhythm and the thing that breaks it
the pack's kill, taken from above

C.title: Off the beat
beats: Vane's Phobos had the line peeled and ready. Then the Roughneck took it.
Pack is one thought. You're a second one.
Nothing in my rhythm is free. You broke it.

B.title: Counting in
beats: Ceil has started waiting for the pack's beat before diving. Most of the time.
I'm counting your rhythm now. Three, then the peel, then me.
Four. You come in on four.

A.title: In time
beats: The pack peeled, the Roughneck came in on four, and the line folded like a door.

motifs: the sniper and the eyes that fly

C.title: Ghosts and drones
beats: Yeva lies in the grass. A drone hums overhead and does not give her away.
Drones already flew it. Your ghosts were where I said.

B.title: Spotting
beats: Noctua's drones mark, Yeva's rifle answers. It has become a conversation.
Two hundred metres, behind the wall, the one with the antenna.
I see the antenna. I'll leave the wall standing. It's pretty.

A.title: Quiet sky
beats: A whole enemy relay went silent and nobody on their side heard a shot.
Your drones are the only noise I like.
Your rifle is the only quiet I trust.

C.title: Whose map
beats: Twenty fleas and twenty-four drones reported the same ridge in the same second.
From the ground. I saw it from the sky.
We speak in plurals. Plurals win.

B.title: Splitting the map
beats: They have divided the map: ground to Tick, sky to Noctua. The border is disputed.
The ridge line is mine. It's high.
The ridge is dirt. Dirt is ours.
Then we both watch it. Twice the eyes.

A.title: Every eye
beats: Nothing moved on the map that the company did not see from two directions.
We counted you in our plurals.
I'll put you in a flight path. It's the nicest thing I know.
